post_title: The Rise of Green Tiles in South Africa: A Trend Reimagined
post_content:
Gone are the days of the bland beige bathroom. With a tombstone that reads, "Here lies Beige, the inoffensive one," it's clear that bold, vibrant choices are taking over modern interiors. Today, green tiles are making a serious comeback, especially in South Africa. Whether it’s a tropical oasis, a Zen-like retreat, or the feel of a lush forest underfoot, green tiles are bringing a sense of rejuvenation to bathrooms everywhere.

Why Green Tiles?

Decor trends might come and go, but the green tile trend in South Africa has deep roots. While the 1970s saw the rise (and fall) of the avocado green bathtub, today's green tiles offer a more versatile, modern touch. Green is a colour that evokes nature, renewal, and peace—everything you need for the ultimate bathroom escape. From mint to moss, sage to emerald, green tiles come in a range of hues that can transform a tired space into something extraordinary.

Let’s explore the top green tile options that are making waves in South Africa.

Mint Green: A Fresh Start

The Alga Liso Matt Tile is the perfect mint green subway tile for a crisp, clean look. Stack them floor-to-ceiling in wet areas like showers for a refreshing vibe that pairs effortlessly with white fixtures, marble countertops, and pale wood finishes. Complement the look with matt black taps and mixers for an extra touch of sophistication.

Curved Green Tiles: Soothing & Stylish

Curved green tiles, such as the Materika Rounded Tile, soften the edges of any bathroom. The deep moss green version of this tile is particularly soothing, offering a natural, earthy vibe. Lay these vertically for a stunning backsplash that adds both texture and colour to your space.

Stripes for Height and Depth

For those looking to add some dimension, green and white striped tiles, like the Home Brick Forest Gloss and Milk Gloss tiles, are a fantastic option. Vertical stripes give the illusion of height, making your bathroom feel more spacious. These glossy tiles create a striking visual contrast, reminiscent of Mediterranean designs with a modern twist.

Touchable Tiles

Textured green tiles are also trending in South Africa, offering a tactile element that invites touch. The Matiz SGN Sea Green Lux Tile is a ribbed, lime-coloured tile that mimics the soft ridges left on the sand by retreating waves. This relief design brings an additional layer of depth to any bathroom wall.

Moody Greens

For a more dramatic aesthetic, consider the Romo Botella Glossy Tile. This bottle-green tile is perfect for creating a glamorous, high-impact bathroom design. The glossy finish reflects light, making the space feel both luxurious and expansive. Pair it with brushed bronze taps to complete the look.

Green Tiles in South Africa: A Lasting Trend

As the demand for stylish, eco-conscious living spaces grows, green tiles are emerging as a hero in modern bathroom design across South Africa. Whether you're creating a serene sanctuary or a bold statement, the wide range of green tile options ensures there’s something to suit every taste. Ready to give your bathroom a green makeover? Start exploring these stunning options today and bring a breath of fresh air into your space.

By focusing on South African consumers' love for modern, nature-inspired design, green tiles are fast becoming a must-have for any stylish home renovation.

post_title: Artful Living, design inspiration for your walls.
post_content:
“It’s not about a tile. It’s about a lifestyle,” says Stevie Joubert, CEO of tile retailer, Stiles. 

Having spent almost 25 years in the tile industry, Stevie is convinced that tiles represent more than just flat, colourful, slabs of porcelain. They represent the lives we want to create and the homes we dream of filling with memories. 

“Your lifestyle is how you live, it reflects who you are,” explains Stevie.  “Your home is an extension of that lifestyle, a gallery where you can craft your own personal masterpiece.” 

Kitchens and bathrooms are often the rooms where homeowners direct their creativity and budget. These are the most lived-in parts of the home, where people wish to make an impression, express themselves and stamp their own personality and style. Our time at home is often scarce and precious. It has a huge impression on our energy and how we function. The rock star chef may want to create the concept kitchen of his dreams. The glamour obsessed might crave a bold statement. Tiles can be conservative, vintage, trendy, bohemian, loud, graphic or luxurious. They can inspire sophistication, serenity or even sustainability. 

“My heart and my passion go into tiles,” says Stevie, “and I’ve got one of the best jobs in the world.” The tile guru has made it his personal mission to search the globe for the most stylish, exclusive and unique products. Joining his father Etienne in the fledgling tile shop in George, in March 2000, Stevie initially focussed strongly on promoting products from South African artisans. Decades later, Stevie’s mandate has grown to establishing relationships with innovative tile and sanitaryware factories across South Africa as well as Europe, South America and Asia. “We want to bring trendsetting tiles into the South African marketplace,” he says simply. 

“A tile is never just a tile,” says Stevie, “a tile is a piece of art.” This is a concept that was impressed upon Stevie by his late father, Etienne. “Art was part of his life,” says Stevie, “he had an eye for craftsmanship. He sketched, painted and made mosaics for most of his life.” An eye for artistry has helped the Stiles team in handpicking their tile and sanitaryware products. “You can see the depth of creativity and the amount of time and energy that went into a well-crafted tile,” explains Stevie. “Tiles also follow fashion,” he elaborates, “they track trends in creativity, style, functionality, texture and even colour. The tiles at Stiles stand apart from others, simply because we prioritise craftsmanship and quality above all else.”

“A tile is something that you will have on your floor for the next fifteen years,” says Stevie, “choosing the best quality product adds value to your home and allows you to live well in your space.” 

“My motivation is simple,” he explains, “the right tile can make someone happy in their own home, and that’s living the dream!”

post_title: Reasons to Choose Rectified Tiles: A Guide to Choosing the Right Flooring For Your Home
post_content:
Flooring is one of the most important decisions you’ll make about your home. A home is a place where you want to feel relaxed and comfortable, and what better way to achieve that than with impressionable surroundings? That is why it’s essential to choose the right flooring for your home. We take a look at why you should choose rectified tiles as your flooring option.   Shop Rectified: 
  • Geotiles Statuary Polished Rectified 600x1200mm 
  • AB Blanco Brillo Rectified 300x900mm
  • Ceusa Confete Pink Natural Rectified 1000x1000mm
What are rectified tiles: 
Rectified tiles are tiles that have been cut to size with precision using specialised equipment, such as a tile rectifying machine. This process results in tiles that are perfectly straight and have precise, uniform dimensions. This makes them easier to install and allows for a more seamless, professional-looking finish. Additionally, because the tiles are cut to exact specifications, they can be installed with very narrow grout lines, which can give the appearance of a larger, more continuous surface. Rectified tiles are often used in high-end installations, such as in luxury homes or commercial buildings, where a precise, professional finish is desired.  Shop Rectified: 
  • Monocibec Charisma Imperial Natural Rectified 600x1200mm 
  • Florim Beton One Chalk Rectified 600x1200mm
  • Monocibec Chiaroscuro Salar Polished Rectified 600x1200mm
What are the advantages? 
Rectified tiles have several advantages over non-rectified tiles. With their very precise cut edges, they can be particularly useful in large installations, where a small mistake in the placement of a tile can be magnified and result in an uneven or unprofessional-looking finish. Additionally, rectified tiles are often of a higher quality than non-rectified tiles, which can be useful in high-end installations where durability and long-lasting performance are important. Finally, rectified tiles can be more versatile in terms of design, as their precise dimensions allow for more complex patterns and layouts to be created.  Additionally, rectified tiles are often used in outdoor installations, such as on patios or pool decks, where their precise dimensions and straight edges can help create a seamless, professional-looking finish. They are also commonly used in wet areas, such as bathrooms and showers, where their precise dimensions and narrow grout lines can help prevent water from seeping behind the tiles and causing damage. Ultimately, the best use of rectified tiles will depend on the specific requirements of your installation and your personal design preferences.  Shop our wide range of rectified tiles in-store and online today at Stiles !

post_title: Buying Tiles: 6 FAQ's to Consider
post_content:
Tiles are a very versatile option for modern interiors. Use it to create hardwearing flooring solutions, or create a fully enclosed tile area such as a patio, bathroom or kitchen. If you’re thinking of tiling your next space, here are some of the top FAQ’s you should consider to help you decide on the best options.

Why choose tiles?

Tiles have been around for thousands of years. In fact, the earliest use of decorative tiles was found in Egypt, dating from about 4000 BC. Not many things continue from one era to the next, so it’s important to consider why tiling is still a preferred option today. Maintenance – What maintenance. Modern tiling options are pretty much maintenance free and will only need a good clean, mop or wipe down to maintain its good looks. (Side note: the more slip resistant a tile is, the harder it is to clean – that said it is still not hard to clean). This is one of the many benefits of tiling a room. It’s hardwearing, resistant to the elements and will most likely last you many many years. Highly Durable – Tiles offer outstanding durability, even in high traffic areas. In fact, modern tiles are created to be stainproof, scratchproof, waterproof, and fire resistant. This means that its potential is endless. Hypoallergenic – As a flooring solution, tiles offer a much more sanitary option when compared to carpets. Germs, bacteria and more do not hold up well on ceramic or porcelain tiled surfaces.

Where will you tile?

From the bathroom surrounds, to the kitchen floors, backsplash and more. Tiles are versatile and a great option in almost any space. Know where you will place your tiles before you head out in search of the right choice. This will help you determine what sort of tile you’ll need.

What’s the difference between floor and wall tiles?

Floor tiles and wall tiles are not equal. You may be able to use a floor tile on a wall, but we do not recommend using wall tiles on your floors. Floor tiles are often created thicker and harder to withstand traffic, appliances and furniture etc. And most have added texture to reduce the risk of slips. Wall tiles, however, are often manufactured as a thinner, smoother and more delicate option. It’s also much slicker when it’s wet, which is why wall tile is not recommended underfoot.

Porcelain or Ceramic tiles?

The biggest difference between porcelain and ceramic tile is the rate at which these absorb water. Porcelain tiles absorb less than 0.5% of water. However, ceramic and other non-porcelain tiles will absorb more. This comes down to what goes into the production of porcelain tiles. The clay is typically denser and so less porous. This makes porcelain tile the perfect option in humid areas like the bathroom. Porcelain tiles are also hardwearing with incredible strength. Furthermore, these can be manufactured to imitate the look of natural materials, such as wood and stone, so they are increasingly used as an affordable alternative to the genuine thing. Ceramic tiles are kiln-fired at a lower temperature than porcelain tiles, making them less dense, softer, and more porous. The clay used to make ceramic tiles is also less refined. This often means it is more affordable than porcelain. Many homeowners opt to install ceramic tiles as flooring, especially in warm climates, where the natural coolness of the tile becomes a welcome perk in the summer months.

How do I choose the right size of tiles?

Depending on your project, the size of your tiles may differ. So which size is best for which space? As a general rule of thumb, choose tiles relative to the size of the room. A lrager space, like an open plan living area, would do well with large format tiles. Smaller areas, like a guest loo or backsplash will most likely handle smaller tiles better. Mosaics are another great option for small surface areas. As a pro tip, remember that your wall tiles should never be larger than their complimentary floor tile as this upsets the proportional look of a room.

How many tiles will I need?

Once you know the actual dimensions of the room, floor, or wall you plan to tile, you can then calculate how many tiles you will need. Many suppliers will provide costing per square metre or will give you the pricing for a box of tiles. Be sure to check which option is provided so you can properly calculate what you need. Remember to also take into account the spacing for grout. We also suggest adding 10% to account for any possible breakage.

Keep it Stylish

Furthermore, they support the local industry, artisans and artists from South Africa. Quality and style will always outweigh price when selecting products. For more visit Stiles.

post_title: Living the dream – The Stiles Story
post_content:
Living the dream

The Stiles Story

If you have ever asked Stevie Joubert, CEO of Stiles, how he is doing, you’d be familiar with his most common answer, “I’m living the dream!” So, what is this dream?
The beginning: When Etienne Joubert, Founder of Stiles, first shared his dream of opening a tile shop in George with his then 21-year-old son, Steve, it fell on pessimistic ears. “As the eldest child, I felt a certain responsibility for my family,” says Steve, “My dad had just been retrenched, he had a family to feed and he was about to use all his savings to buy a store to sell tiles!” Steve, along with his concerns, joined Etienne in what started as a struggling tile shop in George in March 2000.
“Back then, only two wholesalers took a chance on us. It was thanks to them that we were able to push through the stormy beginnings,” says Steve.
 
The relationship between Etienne the visionary and Steve the go-getter created a father-son dynamic that made Stiles a force to be reckoned with. They started with a strong focus on promoting products from local artists. By 2007, Stiles had two branches, and a sanitary ware and plumbing division.
  [caption id="attachment_19994" align="alignnone" width="564"] Etienne Joubert, Founder of Stiles[/caption] Teamwork makes the dream work: At that time, Etienne began handing over more responsibility to Steve. Steve’s first move was to build a strong team to help him take Stiles to the next level. He employed Adele Swart to build the Sanware division of Stiles, Johan (Drom) van Tonder to head up operations, CA, Lili Grobler, to look after the company finances and Nina Appiah-Baiden to grow the marketing. “I have the best team in the Tile and Sanitaryware industry in South Africa! Stiles would be nowhere without them,” says Steve. Living the dream: Fast forward to today and Stiles currently has eight showrooms nationwide along with a wholesale division. Stiles has also absorbed a number of other businesses like Kenzan tiles and most recently Cape Town retailer and wholesaler, Italcotto. “It started as my dad’s dream, but he gave me the opportunity to build that dream,” says Steve, “Now I’m living it! Every day new opportunities are presenting themselves,” he adds. Original article posted on Cape Town, Etc
